name: RANK
description: RANK returns the rank (position) of a number within a list of numbers. It is the legacy rank function, retained for compatibility.
tldr: Gives the rank of a value in a dataset, with ties sharing a rank.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The value whose rank you want to find.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The list (range or array) of numbers to rank against.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Optional. 0 or omitted = descending (largest = rank 1); any nonzero value = ascending (smallest = rank 1).

basicExample.description: Rank of 30 in a descending list
basicExample.explanation: In descending order 50=1, 40=2, 30=3, so 30 is rank 3.

advancedExamples.title: Tied values share the same rank
advancedExamples.scenario: Two equal entries in the list
advancedExamples.description: RANK assigns the same rank to equal values and skips the next rank.
advancedExamples.explanation: The 20s are the 2nd and 3rd largest, so both get rank 2; the 30 then gets rank 4.

advancedExamples.title: Ascending order ranking
advancedExamples.description: Set order to 1 so the smallest number gets rank 1.
advancedExamples.explanation: In ascending order the smallest value, 10, receives rank 1.

howItWorks: RANK compares a value to the other numbers in the reference list. By default (order 0) it ranks from largest to smallest, giving the largest value rank 1; order 1 ranks smallest to largest. Equal values receive the same rank, and the next rank is skipped (e.g. two values at rank 2 leave the next value at rank 4). This tie behavior matches RANK.EQ. In Microsoft 365 use RANK.EQ or RANK.AVG instead.

howToSteps.name: Select the result cell
howToSteps.text: Click where you want the rank.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The rank of the value is returned.

limitations: Tied values share a rank and subsequent ranks are skipped, which can distort percentile-style analysis.
Cannot give fractional (averaged) ranks for ties; use RANK.AVG for that.
Considers only numbers; text in the reference is ignored.

commonErrors.cause: The number is not found in the reference list (or the list has no numbers).
commonErrors.fix: Ensure the value exists in the reference, or rank against the actual data range.

commonErrors.cause: Forgetting the order argument defaults to descending.
commonErrors.fix: Add 1 as the third argument for ascending ranking.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports RANK with the same arguments and behavior as legacy Excel.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Returns 3, identical to Excel. Sheets also offers RANK.AVG and RANK.EQ.

faq.question: What is the difference between RANK and RANK.EQ?
faq.answer: They behave identically. RANK.EQ is the name added in Excel 2010; RANK is kept for compatibility.

faq.question: How do I rank ties with an average rank?
faq.answer: Use RANK.AVG, which assigns tied values their average rank (e.g. 2.5 instead of 2).

faq.question: Why are ranks skipped after a tie?
faq.answer: RANK gives both tied values the same rank, so if two share rank 2, the next distinct value becomes rank 4.
